narration.text: Air is 78% nitrogen, but plants can't use it.
Bacteria must fix it into usable forms first.
Lightning fixes 5 to 10 billion kilograms a year.
But most fixation is done by bacteria.
Ocean phytoplankton rely on cyanobacteria to fix it for them.
Combustion has raised nitrogen oxide flux 6 to 7 times.
If fixation stopped, soils and seas would slowly starve.
So the air's most common gas is useless until microbes change it.
